name: Compressed and liquid air energy storage
aliases: Compressed and liquid air energy storage
applications: reuse of salt caverns and mines
principle: Air is compressed (CAES) into a cavern or vessel, or liquefied (LAES), and later expanded through a turbine; advanced designs store the compression heat to avoid burning gas. Hydrostor's Willow Rock project in California is 500 MW and 4,000 MWh (8+ hours) of advanced CAES with a 50+ year design life.

process_steps.name: Compress air using surplus power, storing the heat
Store air in cavern or tank
Expand air with stored heat through turbine
